clue.text: Look more impressive having dismissed first of Republicans

indicators.note: dismissing a letter sends it out of the word

parts.note: grander means statelier, more impressive

indicators.note: the opening letter of Republicans is the one taken

explanation.surface: A politician seems more impressive once the leading Republican has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look more impressive' reads as one verb phrase, but 'Look' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a gander is informal British slang for having a look at something.

clue.text: Group of nations supporting aid fixed for so long

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath the other
the word aid is fixed, rearranged

parts.note: the EU, European Union, is a group of nations

explanation.surface: European nations prop up a long-arranged aid package.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are ways of saying goodbye; 'so long' is a casual farewell.

clue.text: Abandon revolutionary sailor and soldier

parts.note: to desert is to abandon

indicators.note: the sailor word revolves, read backwards

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A rebel sailor and a soldier walk out together.
explanation.definitionFit: The Desert Rats were British soldiers of the 7th Armoured Division in North Africa.

clue.text: Dangerous raid, oddly, on broadcaster

indicators.note: take the odd-numbered letters of raid

parts.note: Sky is a British television broadcaster

explanation.surface: A hazardous raid is carried out on a television company.
explanation.definitionFit: Something risky carries danger, so it is hazardous.

clue.text: What might be left, say, in frilly surroundings

indicators.note: with 'surroundings', places one piece within the frilly word
the frilly word forms the surroundings that enclose the other piece

parts.note: lacy means decorated with frills of lace
e.g. (for example) is what 'say' means in 'a fruit, say'

explanation.surface: Something left behind, perhaps, wrapped in lacy trimmings.
explanation.definitionFit: A bequest in a will is something left to someone after a death.

clue.text: Biographical tales about new vital means of communication?

parts.note: a life is a biography, as in a life of Dickens

indicators.note: the tales word goes about, around, the new letter

parts.note: tales can mean lies, as in telling tales

explanation.surface: Biographers' stories reworked as essential communication channels.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifeline is a crucial link or support, such as a rope or a vital contact with others.

clue.text: Person who's invited may be judged in hearing

indicators.note: the word for judged is as heard spoken, not as spelt

parts.note: guessed means judged, estimated

explanation.surface: Someone invited may be put on trial at a court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearing' looks like a court case, but signals a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A guest is someone who has been invited to a home or event.

clue.text: Furiously tail chap pinching old banger

indicators.note: the rearranged letters pinch, take in, the old letter
the words tail chap are worked furiously into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone angrily pursues a man who has stolen an old car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banger' is British slang for both an old car and a sausage; here it is the sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: A chipolata is a small thin sausage, and banger is British slang for a sausage.

clue.text: What's left after following schedule is cut short?

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: the schedule word loses its final letter

parts.note: an agenda is a schedule of business

explanation.surface: What remains after a timetable has been trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: A fag end is the stub of a cigarette, or the last remnant of something.

clue.text: Spies found in a men's toilet

parts.note: the Gents is British slang for a men's public lavatory

explanation.surface: Secret agents meet furtively in a public lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Agents are operatives of an intelligence service, i.e. spies.

clue.text: Name adopted when following boxer

indicators.note: the word for when comes after the boxer's name

parts.note: Muhammad Ali, the famous heavyweight boxer
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A fighter takes a new name to follow on from a famous boxer.
explanation.walkthrough: Cassius Clay famously adopted the name Ali, which sharpens the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An alias is an assumed name used in place of one's real one.

clue.text: Many a time beset by evil — good to be mollifying

indicators.note: a word beset by another is surrounded by it

parts.note: sin is wrongdoing, evil
often means many a time

explanation.surface: Repeated temptation by evil reads as a sermon on goodness calming people down.
explanation.definitionFit: Softening someone's anger is calming or appeasing them, which is what mollifying does.

clue.text: Person serving Queen may see European question about resistance

indicators.note: the question goes about, around, the resistance letter

parts.note: a query is a question
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: A royal attendant meets a European asking about resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: An equerry is an officer of the British royal household who attends a member of the royal family.

clue.text: Disappointed and allowed to drink in one

parts.note: let means allowed
to down a drink is to drink it in one go

explanation.surface: Someone feels deflated even though they were permitted to down a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To be let down is to be disappointed by someone failing you.

clue.text: Detective reading for fun

parts.note: DI is Detective Inspector
a reading of a text is one version or interpretation of it

explanation.surface: A detective reads crime fiction for pleasure.
explanation.definitionFit: A diversion is an amusement or pastime, something done for entertainment.

clue.text: Criminal sold a vice that's articulated

indicators.note: criminal here signals the letters are bent out of order

explanation.surface: A crook peddled a vice and talked about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To vocalise something is to utter it aloud, to articulate it.

clue.text: Instant act as broker to support firm regularly

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece goes below the one it holds up
take every other letter of the word firm

parts.note: to mediate is to broker an agreement between parties

explanation.surface: A go-between steps in at once to prop up a company.
explanation.definitionFit: Immediate and instant both describe something happening at once, without delay.

clue.text: Raises game and strikes

definitions.meaning: on a shoot, beaters thrash bushes to drive birds into the air
hits, as in hitting a drum or a person

explanation.surface: A sportsperson improves their play and lands blows.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to rouse game birds by thrashing cover and to hit repeatedly.

clue.text: Officer's new bride touring Baltic port

indicators.note: the rearranged letters tour, go around, the port
the word bride is made new, rearranged

parts.note: Riga is the Latvian capital and a Baltic seaport

explanation.surface: An officer's fresh bride is sightseeing around a Baltic city.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigadier is a senior army officer, ranking above a colonel.

clue.text: Expert appearing in newspaper feature

indicators.note: the expert word appears in the middle of the newspaper's letters

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times newspaper
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A specialist is featured in a newspaper article.
explanation.definitionFit: A facet is an aspect or feature of something.

clue.text: German wife and son outside Germany must be impostors

indicators.note: the wife and son sit outside, around, the Germany letter

parts.note: Frau is German for wife
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A German family abroad turn out to be fakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Frauds are people pretending to be what they are not, i.e. impostors.

clue.text: Is cat meat made to chew?

indicators.note: these letters are made into something new, rearranged

explanation.surface: A cheeky question: is cat food what someone has been forced to eat?
explanation.definitionFit: To masticate is to chew food thoroughly.

clue.text: Emirates will be empty, hosting opening occasions

indicators.note: the outer letters host, take in, the opening
emptying the word leaves only its outer letters

parts.note: a vent is an opening

explanation.surface: An airline's planes fly empty while it hosts launch parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Events are happenings or occasions.

clue.text: Informed by a couple of students taking everything into account

indicators.note: the informed word sits by, beside, the student letters

parts.note: L for learner is a student, so two of them give two Ls
told means informed

explanation.surface: Someone learns something from a pair of students.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in total, when everything is reckoned up.

clue.text: Love playing game that's last of series

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

indicators.note: the word game is played with, rearranged

explanation.surface: A romance in play during a game that ends a series.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, so the end of a sequence.

clue.text: Tramp stumbles across area with last of booze

indicators.note: the stumbling word stretches across, around, the area letter

parts.note: trips means stumbles

indicators.note: only the final letter of booze is used

explanation.surface: A down-and-out staggers about clutching the dregs of a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tramp' looks like a noun for a vagrant, but it is a verb meaning to trudge.
explanation.definitionFit: To traipse is to walk wearily or reluctantly, which is how one tramps along.

clue.text: Subject of note crossing border

indicators.note: the note spans across, around, the border word

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale
a hem is the border of a garment

explanation.surface: A notable person is subject to crossing a frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the subject of a talk, piece of writing or composition.

clue.text: Article written for bishop on board perhaps

definitions.meaning: an article in a newspaper is a written item
a bishop is one of the men on a chessboard

explanation.surface: A journalist writes about a clergyman serving on a board of directors.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a written article and a chessman such as a bishop.

clue.text: Pressing new peers in appointment

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go in the appointment word

parts.note: a date is an arranged appointment

indicators.note: the word peers is made new, rearranged

explanation.surface: Urgent business: new members of the Lords arrive for a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pressing' looks like a verb, but it is an adjective meaning urgent; 'new' rearranges the lords to ESPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperate or pressing need is one that is urgent and extreme.

clue.text: Incompetent writer backed by one with time

indicators.note: the reversed writer comes after, by, the one

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the writer word is backed, written backwards

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A useless author is supported by somebody with time to spare.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone inept lacks skill, so is incompetent at the task.

clue.text: A challenge to accept women's promotion on the web

indicators.note: the challenge word accepts, takes in, the women letter

parts.note: a dare is a challenge
W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: A campaign challenges a company to take on women in senior roles.
explanation.definitionFit: Adware is software that pushes advertising at internet users.

clue.text: Student failing to start easy cash job

indicators.note: the word fails to start, losing its opening letter

parts.note: a learner is a student

explanation.surface: A student who never gets going takes a job for quick money.
explanation.definitionFit: A 'nice little earner' is British slang for a profitable, easy source of income.
